screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.apply_a: Apply a translucent purple field with drifting magenta pixels. Field and particle colors can also be edited separately.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.checked: Checked: apply blocking in this movement direction. Unchecked: allow passage in this direction.
Checked: damage matching entities approaching in this world direction. Downward applies from above, including entities standing on a horizontal bridge. Unchecked: no damage in this direction.
Checked: detect crossings in this movement direction. Unchecked: ignore them.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.choose_: Choose the group's default rules, or select one outgoing field for different Blocking, Detection and Damage filters. A field-specific rule takes priority over defaults. All three filters can differ for one field; energy, color and redstone output remain group settings. Changes apply automatically; switching loads that field's saved settings.
Choose hex lattice, a clean translucent glow, drifting colored pixels, or plasma. All styles retain impact ripples. Visuals do not change filters or collision.

Choose how dropped item stacks affect the crossing counter. Count each stack: a stack of 64 adds one. Count each item: it adds 64. Mobs and players always count once. Detection output is unaffected: every crossing sends one pulse, however much crosses at once.

Choose how long each detection pulse stays on. There is a 0.1-second off gap between queued pulses so counters see separate events. Times assume Minecraft's normal 20 ticks per second. Pulse mode must be enabled on Detection.

Choose how the tower builds its hollow shell: opposing laser curtains, a rising ring, assembling hex cells, meridian arcs, a crown seed, or plasma dissolve. Works with every pattern. All take four seconds; collision starts only when complete. This choice does not change filters or power use.
Choose short vanilla sound effects: Soft sizzle, Crystal or Electric. No new music or continuous sound loop is added.

Choose the orientation of the flat field between these rails. Wall facing North / South is crossed north-to-south; Wall facing East / West is crossed east-to-west. Horizontal floor / ceiling is crossed upward or downward. Only orientations compatible with the rail placement are offered.
Choose where the enable/disable signal is read. Any side reads every face except the output side. Top and Bottom refer to the emitter block; North, South, East and West are world directions.

Choose the travel direction to edit. North → South means entering from the north and leaving to the south. All directions edits the shared fallback; custom directional rules take priority. Blocking, detection and damage are independent.

Choose when a powered field operates: always, only while its redstone input is on, or only while that input is off. Redstone switches the field; it never powers it. Every emitter and rail needs FE from an energy mod.

Choose where to connect redstone dust, a lamp or a counter. The detector sends its output through this side of the source emitter. A rail chain shares one detector output at the coordinates shown below. Input and output must use different sides.
%1$sChoose whether matching entities or everything outside the selection takes damage. Skip owner always takes priority.
Choose who can change this connected network's settings. Management permission is separate from permission to pass through the field.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.click_t: Click to cycle: Any age, Babies only, Adults only. Babies are living entities Minecraft marks as babies; Adults means living entities that are not babies. Dropped items and other nonliving entities need Any age.

Click to cycle. Off: no detection output. Pulse on crossing: send one redstone pulse when a matching entity completely passes through. On while touching: keep redstone on while a matching entity overlaps the field. Touching alone does not count as a crossing.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.copy_th: Copy the entity type sampled with your tuner into this filter. An enabled Player list takes priority for players.

Copy the entity type saved in your tuner, for example all cows rather than one particular cow. First sneak-right-click a living mob, or air for players. This replaces the current filter details. Changes apply immediately.

Copy the individual saved in your tuner. Sneak-right-click a living mob to sample it, or sneak-right-click air to sample yourself. This replaces the current filter details with that individual's UUID. Changes apply immediately.
Copy the individual UUID sampled with your tuner into this filter. An enabled Player list takes priority for players.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.custom_: Custom color for impact effects, drifting pixels, plasma veins and fizzle bursts. Used only while Effect color is set to Custom accent. Enter six hex digits, such as FF33CC for magenta.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.cycle_s: Cycle Sweep, Dissolve, Fade, or the six projection styles. On walls the ring becomes a rising scan line and meridians become tracing ribs. On floors and ceilings they travel across the surface. Projection styles form for four seconds before blocking, detecting or damaging; the original three modes keep their progressive activation.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.drops_s: %1$sDrops selects loose item entities, such as gunpowder on the ground. Use the Dropped item box for a specific item. Use Any age.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.emitter: Emitter face that sends the sensor's redstone signal. The input never reads this face. This is a physical block face, not an entity's travel direction.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.enable_: Enable contact damage using this tab's own filter. Blocking and detection remain independent. Damage starts off; enabling it can hurt selected players, mobs and damageable nonliving entities.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.enter_0: Enter 0 to 1000 health points per successful hit. 2 HP equals one heart. Damage is off by default. Vanilla invulnerability, damage immunity and protection mods still apply. Nonliving entities respond only if Minecraft gives them damage behavior; this never forcibly deletes an entity.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.enter_a: Enter a six-digit color code, for example 52E5FF for cyan. You can also choose a color preset above. Valid color changes apply automatically.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.entitie: %1$sEntities outside that selection trigger detection. Skip owner: Yes always excludes the owner. This does not change what the field blocks.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.hostile: %1$sHostile selects entities Minecraft classifies as monsters, such as zombies and creepers.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.how_lon: How long each crossing pulse stays on. A short off interval separates queued pulses so counters can distinguish them. Used with Pulse on crossing.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.immedia: Immediately clear the recorded crossing count, recent detection and waiting pulses.
Immediately use this color preset for the emitter(s) selected in Connections.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.inspect: Inspect carried inventory using a separate player and item filter. Detect contraband, deny passage, drop it, or transfer it to adjacent storage. Badge and management permissions remain separate.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.issue_b: Issue badges for access groups and revoke them when needed. Add an access group to a player filter to use its badges. A badge does not grant management permission.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.leave_b: Leave blank for no additional restriction. Valid changes apply automatically.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.manage_: Manage up to 64 dropped-item IDs or item tags. Drag item icons from your inventory, JEI or EMI into the boxes without consuming anything. Whitelist allows listed drops; blacklist blocks listed drops. Detection and damage have their own lists. Item lists ignore mob age and general inversion.

Manage up to 64 mob IDs or entity-type tags using whitelist/blacklist modes. Drag spawn eggs into the boxes or type IDs. Age, individual UUID and custom label narrow the listed selection. Players and dropped items have separate lists. Rules belong to the selected travel direction.

Manage up to 64 players by Minecraft account name or UUID. Choose a whitelist or blacklist for blocking, or listed/unlisted players for detection and damage. A list changes players only, respects this direction and Skip owner, and replaces the other filter details for players.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.master_: Master switch for this emitter's activation, deactivation, impact and fizzle sounds. Minecraft's Blocks volume also controls these effects. No looping background hum.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.matches: Matches field keeps impacts, pixels, plasma veins and fizzle effects in the field's color. Custom accent lets you choose their color separately below. Formation beams keep the field color.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.matchin: %1$sMatching entities are blocked. Everything else may pass. Click to switch to allowing only the selection.
%1$sMatching entities trigger detection. Blocking is configured separately in Blocking.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.minimum: Minimum time between successful field hits on one entity, shared across touching tiles and overlapping fields so seams cannot multiply damage. Vanilla damage cooldowns still apply.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.no_hide: No hides the forcefield graphics only. Blocking, detection and damage continue while powered. Use Field: Off on the Overview tab to stop operation.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.nonlivi: %1$sNonliving selects the remaining entities, such as arrows, boats, minecarts and XP orbs. Dropped items have their own Drops category. Use Any age.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.on_allo: On allows the group to operate when it has energy and satisfies its redstone condition. Off stops its fields. Like every setting here, it applies to all of your connected emitters and rails.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.only_ma: %1$sOnly matching entities may pass; everything else is blocked. Example: check Passive and Babies only to allow baby passive mobs through. Skip owner: Yes always lets the owner pass.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.optiona: Optional: enter minecraft:gunpowder to match dropped gunpowder, or #minecraft:logs to match dropped logs. Check Drops above and use Any age. This checks items on the ground, not a mob's or player's inventory. One ID or existing item tag per box; blank means any dropped item.

Optional: enter one entity type, such as minecraft:creeper. Or enter an existing entity-type tag, such as #yourpack:guards, to match a group defined by a mod or datapack. The # is required for groups; typing a name does not create a group. Keep its category checked above. Leave blank to accept any type in the selected categories.

Optional: match a label assigned to an entity with Minecraft's /tag command. For example, /tag @s add resident gives you the label resident; enter resident here, without #. This is different from an entity-type or item group. Leave blank to ignore custom labels.

Optional: match one specific entity using its unique UUID. Easier: sneak-right-click a living mob with the tuner, or sneak-right-click air to sample yourself. Then click Sample individual. An enabled Player list replaces this restriction for players.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.passive: %1$sPassive selects living entities that are not players or monsters, such as cows, sheep and villagers. Neutral mobs can belong here even when angry.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.players: %1$sPlayers selects player characters. Skip owner controls whether this emitter's owner can match.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.selecte: Selected means any checked category that also meets EVERY filled-in detail below. Blank details add no restriction. Enabled player, mob and item lists use their own modes instead.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.set_hor: Set horizontal mode, block all entities moving downward (including the owner), allow upward passage and disable damage. Replaces blocking direction overrides. Use on connected rails to build a walkable bridge.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.sets_a_: Sets a purple field with drifting pixels and explicitly enables a magenta custom accent.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.shared_: Shared uses the All directions filter. Click to create a Custom copy for this travel direction, then edit it below. Click again to remove the override and use Shared. Changing shared rules does not change custom copies.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.short_c: Short colored bursts on damage and a larger body-shaped burst on a lethal hit. Effects are capped per tick and emitter. This changes particles, not damage or sounds.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.show_wi: Show with tuner displays movement arrows while holding the tuner or briefly previewing a connection. Amber means blocking is enabled in that direction; green means it is disabled. Filters still determine which entities are blocked. Hidden removes these guides. This preference is saved for your client only.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.to_sout: %1$sTo South means traveling from north to south; Upward means moving from below to above. These are world directions, not the direction you are looking. Entity filters still apply.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.toggle_: Toggle the moving pattern on the field surface. This does not disable projection/retraction or hardware animations.
Toggle this sound category independently. The master All field sounds switch must also be on.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.yes_add: Yes adds real Minecraft block light. No keeps the surroundings dark for mob farms. The field can still look bright and block entities when world lighting is off.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.yes_alw: Yes always allows the player who placed this emitter through, even with Allow selected only. No applies the normal blocking rules to the owner too.
Yes always exempts the emitter owner from damage, including inverted filters. No includes the owner when they match.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.yes_nev: Yes never detects the player who placed this emitter. No includes that player when they match the detection rules.
screen.fieldemitters.fieldclient.this_fi: This field is private. Ask its owner for management access.

screen.fieldemitters.management.lookup_t: Lookup timed out. Try again or enter a UUID.
screen.fieldemitters.management.minecraf: Minecraft account name or UUID; server nicknames are not supported.
screen.fieldemitters.management.only_the: Only the owner can change management permissions.
screen.fieldemitters.management.only_you: Only you and server operators can change these permissions.
screen.fieldemitters.management.these_pe: These permissions control field settings, not passage. Badges never grant management rights. Public mode lets any player change field settings.
screen.fieldemitters.playerlist.list_mod: List modes replace the general filter for players only. Mob and item rules stay as configured. Movement directions and Skip owner still apply.
screen.fieldemitters.playerlist.player_a: Player added. Choose the list mode above to enable it.

screen.fieldemitters.playerlist.use_a_mi: Use a Minecraft account name, not a server nickname. Names resolve to UUIDs; UUIDs remain valid after a name change. Offline-mode identities depend on the server.

screen.fieldemitters.remote.name_this_en: Name this entire connected field. Changes apply automatically. Blank restores its location-based name. The origin stays at the first known emitter even when that emitter is unloaded.
screen.fieldemitters.remote.no_loaded_fi: No loaded fields available to you here.
screen.fieldemitters.remote.open_this_em: Open this emitter's controls. Connections selects one connection or your entire connected field.

screen.fieldemitters.typelist.drag_from_: Drag from your inventory, JEI or EMI into a filter box.

screen.fieldemitters.typelist.dropped_it: Dropped items only; players and mobs keep their own rules.
screen.fieldemitters.typelist.general_fi: General filter preserves the existing category and single-type rule. List modes override categories, single-type rules and general inversion for this kind of entity only. Direction and Skip owner still apply. Mob age, UUID and custom label narrow the listed selection before whitelist/blacklist is applied.
screen.fieldemitters.typelist.item_id_mi: Item ID: minecraft:gunpowder. Item tag: #minecraft:logs. For checkpoints, matches carried inventory items; otherwise matches dropped item entities. Item count and components are ignored.
screen.fieldemitters.typelist.matching_i: Matching items carried by selected players are contraband.
screen.fieldemitters.typelist.mob_id_min: Mob ID: minecraft:creeper. Entity-type tag: #minecraft:skeletons. Drag a spawn egg to add its mob type. This is not a /tag label. Players have their own list.
screen.fieldemitters.typelist.mobs_only_: Mobs only; age, UUID and label narrow the listed selection.
screen.fieldemitters.typelist.right_clic: Right-click a filter icon to remove it.
screen.fieldemitters.typelist.the_previo: The previous single-type restriction. Only used in General filter mode; blank means any type. Changes apply after a short typing pause.
screen.fieldemitters.typelist.use_a_spaw: Use a spawn egg for a mob, or type its ID above.
screen.fieldemitters.typelist.your_inven: Your inventory (drag a copy into the boxes)
screen.fieldemitters.control.no_energy_c: No energy. Connect an FE cable, generator or energy cell from another mod.
screen.fieldemitters.control.not_enough_: Not enough energy. This group needs %1$s FE per tick.
screen.fieldemitters.control.waiting_for: Powered. Waiting for the redstone condition.
screen.fieldemitters.control.use_group_r: Use the group rules for this field
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.drop_th: Drop the rules kept for this one field so it follows the group again. Both ends of the field forget them. Shown only while a field has rules of its own.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.world_d: World directions name the way an entity travels, so each side of a perimeter needs its own setting. Relative names the crossing as entering or leaving the area the posts enclose, so one setting reads correctly on every side at once and stays correct if you move or rotate the perimeter. Relative is offered only where the posts enclose an area, and it uses the shared rule rather than per-direction rules.
screen.fieldemitters.controlhelp.outside: Outside → Inside covers entities entering the area the posts enclose; Inside → Outside covers entities leaving it. Each span works out which of its own faces is the inside, so one setting reads correctly on every side of the perimeter.
